description: Before-and-after measure of PAPER-95, Emma Bovary: 12 facts of her life asked about in a public quiz on the novel that the owner found, put in our own words, without its choices, and checked in the book. Kept apart: their subjects were not chosen by whoever wrote the other questions; they are famous episodes, and some were also asked while the defaults were tuned.

items.input: What had happened to your father when Charles was first called to your farm?
Which marquis invited you to a ball, and to what place?
passageQuotes: invited by the Marquis d'Andervilliers to Vaubyessard

items.input: When you first met Léon at Yonville, what was his work?
items.expectedOutput: He was a clerk at the notary's, Monsieur Guillaumin.
passageQuotes: a clerk at the notary's, Monsieur Guillaumin

items.input: Why did your husband urge you to accept the rides on horseback that Rodolphe offered?
items.expectedOutput: For your health, which came before everything.

items.input: How did the letter in which Rodolphe gave you up reach you?
items.expectedOutput: At the bottom of a basket of apricots, under vine leaves, brought by his ploughman Girard.
passageQuotes: had a basket of apricots picked

items.input: How did the operation your husband performed on Hippolyte's foot end?
items.expectedOutput: In gangrene: Doctor Canivet amputated the leg at the thigh.
passageQuotes: amputation of the thigh by Doctor Canivet

items.input: When you fell ill after that letter, for how long did your husband stay by you?
passageQuotes: For forty-three days Charles did not leave her

items.input: At the opera in Rouen, what did the love you saw on the stage make you feel about your own life?
items.expectedOutput: She recognised the rapture and anguish that had almost killed her, and felt no one had ever loved her with such a love.
passageQuotes: no one on earth had loved her with such love

items.input: When you and Léon left the cathedral, how did you spend the following hours?
items.expectedOutput: Shut in a cab with the blinds drawn, driving on and on through Rouen.

items.input: What did you tell your husband you needed in town every week, and why did you really go?
items.expectedOutput: Piano lessons; in fact to see her lover, Léon.
passageQuotes: permission to go to town once a week to see her lover

items.input: What did the official paper left at your house demand of you, and how quickly?
items.expectedOutput: To pay eight thousand francs within twenty-four hours, or her furniture would be seized.
passageQuotes: To pay the sum of eight thousand francs

items.input: When nobody would lend you the money, what did you do at the chemist's?
items.expectedOutput: She took arsenic from the blue jar in his storeroom and ate it.
